objective:
Teach the deterministic time resolver weekday + part-of-day phrases such as "Saturday morning", so "Mowed Saturday morning." is dated instead of going to review.

BACKGROUND (read the code):
- `core-domain/.../temporal/TemporalResolver.kt` resolves the model's verbatim `temporalExpression` by an ordered table of whole-phrase regex rules (RULES), documented as ADR-028 in docs/DECISIONS.md. Relevant existing pieces: the `Band` enum (MORNING 05-12 anchor 09:00, AFTERNOON 12-17 anchor 15:00, EVENING 17-21 anchor 19:00, TONIGHT 17-24 anchor 21:00), `band(word)`, rule 3 "yesterday (morning|afternoon|evening)" -> band anchor on yesterday, APPROXIMATE; rule 6 "last night" -> yesterday 21:00; rule 10 weekday, optionally "last <weekday>" -> start of the most recent previous such day, never today (same weekday as today = 7 days ago), DATE_ONLY (that 'never today' rule is an owner decision and must not change). Normalization already lowercases, trims edge punctuation and drops one leading filler (on/at/about/around/approximately); a hedge keeps/softens precision.
- Today "Saturday morning" matches no rule -> Unresolvable -> the capture goes to review.
- The semantic corpus (`core-testing/src/main/resources/semantic-corpus/corpus.json`) case `time-mowed-saturday-morning` (captured 2026-09-15T20:00-04:00, America/Detroit, a Tuesday) expects resolvedLocalDate 2026-09-12, precision APPROXIMATE, and carries a `knownResolverGap` field. `CorpusTemporalTest` (core-testing tests) requires the set of cases that do not resolve as expected to equal EXACTLY the set marked `knownResolverGap`, so once the resolver is fixed that field must be removed or the test fails. docs/SEMANTIC_CORPUS.md explains this and currently names this case as the one known gap. corpus.json must stay LF-only (its exact bytes are hashed); edit it without changing line endings or any other bytes than removing that one field (and the comma before it).

DO:
1. Add one rule to RULES, placed next to the weekday rule (before it is fine; matching is whole-phrase): `(?:last )?<weekday> (morning|afternoon|evening|night)` -> the same date the weekday rule would pick (most recent previous such day, never today), at the part-of-day anchor: morning 09:00, afternoon 15:00, evening 19:00, night 21:00 (reuse Band; 'night' uses the TONIGHT band's 21:00 anchor, matching 'last night'). Precision APPROXIMATE. Factor the weekday date calculation into a small shared helper so the two rules cannot drift. Update the rule-number comments sensibly.
2. Tests in TemporalResolverTest: each of morning/afternoon/evening/night for a weekday earlier in the week; 'last <weekday> <band>' gives the same answer; the same weekday as today gives 7 days ago (e.g. 'Tuesday morning' said on a Tuesday evening); a leading 'on' and a hedge ('about Saturday morning') still work and stay APPROXIMATE; the result is in the capture's zone (use a non-UTC zone such as America/Detroit and one DST-transition week if the existing tests have a pattern for it); existing weekday-only and 'yesterday morning' behaviour unchanged; a phrase like 'saturday brunch' is still Unresolvable.
3. corpus.json: remove the `knownResolverGap` field from `time-mowed-saturday-morning` only (keep its note). Keep the file LF-only.
4. docs/DECISIONS.md ADR-028: add the new row to the rule table (after the weekday row, or wherever the rule sits in order): "weekday + morning/afternoon/evening/night, optionally 'last …'" -> band anchor on the day the weekday rule picks (night = 21:00) -> APPROXIMATE, and mention it in the Status line as added 2026-09-19 (FX1.2).
5. docs/SEMANTIC_CORPUS.md: update the passage (around the CorpusTemporalTest description, and anywhere else) that says 'Mowed Saturday morning' is the one known resolver gap -- there are now none; keep the explanation of how knownResolverGap works for future cases.

PRIVACY (AGENTS.md #11): no logging.

DEVICE SAFETY: no device needed. Never run adb, installDebug or any connected* task. Set ANDROID_SERIAL=none-for-this-task in the environment of every Gradle command.

No new phrases beyond weekday + morning/afternoon/evening/night (no 'Saturday at noon', 'yesterday night', 'this Saturday', dates with times).

All existing TemporalResolver behaviour is unchanged; existing tests pass unmodified.
New TemporalResolverTest cases cover DO 2 and pass.
corpus.json differs from HEAD only by the removed knownResolverGap field (and its preceding comma) and stays LF-only; CorpusTemporalTest passes with no known gaps.
ADR-028's table and status line and SEMANTIC_CORPUS.md reflect the new rule and the cleared gap.
